# CANDIDATE: EXECUTION_PATH_ACCOUNTING_GUARD

**Filed:** 2026-07-22
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)
**Type:** quality_gate
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

We propose to add a periodic guard (e.g., a pytest or script) that scans all execution monitors/funnels (fill_funnel.py, state dashboards, etc.) for missing accounting of the `extra_exec` list, ensuring any new execution path is tallied in enter/attempted/accepted counts. This guard will be integrated into the CI pipeline to prevent future blind spots in execution accounting.

## Mechanism

The guard will statically analyze the specified execution monitor/funnel files (e.g., fill_funnel.py, any state dashboard files) to verify that every execution path that increments the `enter`, `attempted`, or `accepted` counters also properly accounts for the `extra_exec` list. Specifically, it will check that whenever a new execution path is added (e.g., a new condition that leads to an increment), the `extra_exec` list is updated accordingly to reflect the new path in the tallies. The guard will fail the CI build if any execution path is found that increments counters without updating `extra_exec`.

## OP-20 disclosures

1. **Account-size assumption:** N/A (this guard is a code quality check and does not involve trading or account sizing).
2. **Sample bias:** The guard scans all execution monitors/funnels (fill_funnel.py, state dashboards, etc.) in the codebase. The sample is the entire set of these files as of the guard's implementation. Selection method is static analysis of the specified files. Overfit risk is low as the guard checks for a specific coding pattern (accounting of `extra_exec`) and does not depend on historical data.
3. **Out-of-sample:** NEEDS-OOS (the guard has not yet been run in CI; its effectiveness in catching future blind spots will be validated by its ability to prevent similar issues in future PRs).
4. **Real-fills:** NEEDS-REAL-FILLS (the guard does not alter the trading engine, so real-fills behavior on J days is unchanged; any changes would come from fixes triggered by the guard, which are out of scope for this proposal).
5. **Failure modes:** 
   - False positive: guard flags a correct accounting as missing due to overly strict pattern matching.
   - False negative: guard misses a missing accounting due to complex code patterns (e.g., dynamic increments).
   - Guard itself fails due to an exception, causing CI to fail incorrectly.
   - Guard becomes outdated if new execution monitor/funnel files are added and not included in the scan.
6. **Concentration:** N/A (this guard does not produce P&L; concentration disclosure is not applicable).

## Pre-merge gate

- The guard must pass unit tests that verify its ability to detect missing accounting in controlled test cases.
- The guard must be integrated into the CI pipeline (e.g., added to the test suite that runs on every PR).
- The guard must not produce false negatives on a set of known-good execution paths (to be defined in the guard's test suite).
- The guard must not produce false positives on a set of known-bad execution paths (i.e., it should only flag when accounting is truly missing).

## Confidence

8 / 10 -- The mechanism is straightforward and addresses a specific, well-defined problem (missing accounting of `extra_exec`). Similar guards have been effective in preventing regressions in other parts of the codebase. The main risk is in the implementation of the static analysis (could miss complex patterns), but this can be mitigated with thorough unit tests.

## Pre-existing leaderboard impact

This candidate does not conflict with any existing candidates in the leaderboard as it is a non-trading code quality guard. It complements all candidates by helping ensure that future trading strategy changes (candidates 1-25) do not introduce blind spots in execution accounting.
